title: The browser activation chain installs the policy, so project.activate stops refusing ACTIVATION_POLICY_UNMEASURED
description:
Filed by worker-d6e44333 on 2026-09-05 from task-ac9d5e2d43334525bd990b1362652ce4 (the browser-only fresh-start proof row), which found this with a REAL daemon at `seed: "NONE"`. The owning row is task-3506e04abcef4fc3a69299ca238ae1b3 (DONE, the Activate card); full evidence is comment-f64e380cbb614b9cad68ff6bda0c755a there. task-ac9d5e2d is BLOCKED on this row: it cannot prove a browser-only fresh start that does not complete.

THE DEFECT, measured not inferred. On a genuinely empty store the browser Activate chain runs three steps green and then refuses:
  Activate the project - refused ACTIVATION_POLICY_UNMEASURED @ DAEMON_ACTIVATION_RECEIPTS
(`cr.activate.step.project.activate` carries data-ok="false"; register, bind_repository and provider.probe all carry "true".)

WHY. `ACTIVATION_CHAIN_KINDS` (apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/activation-port.ts:29) is [project.register, project.bind_repository, provider.probe, project.activate] and deliberately mirrors `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES` (apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-sequence.ts:31-35), which for project.activate lists only those three. But the activation witness is minted from MEASURED receipts and the `policy` receipt is the digest of the INSTALLED SLICE SET (activation-receipts.ts:38). Nothing installed means nothing to measure, so the activate refuses. A fresh `POST /activation/read` returns blocking:["provider","policy"]; provider.probe clears provider and nothing in the browser chain clears policy. `POST /affordances/read` on that same fresh store offers policy.install, so the daemon is offering the step the card never dispatches.

task-4b9c394d made the policy receipt load-bearing and updated DEMO_SEED_KINDS - demo-seed-plan.ts:91-95 spells the whole failure out, "Measured against a live daemon, not reasoned" - but did not update COMMAND_PREREQUISITES, so every consumer deriving a chain from that table still omits the step.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: every other lane seeds, and DEMO_SEED_KINDS installs policy before activate, so the receipt is always already measured. Only `seed: "NONE"` exposes it.

THE DESIGN CALL IS DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN, because it is not a worker's to make silently: (a) add "policy.install" to COMMAND_PREREQUISITES["project.activate"] so every derived chain gains it, at the cost of changing a shared table with other consumers; or (b) add it to ACTIVATION_CHAIN_KINDS alone, which contradicts that constant's own docblock about holding no preference of its own. Whoever plans this must enumerate the consumers of COMMAND_PREREQUISITES before choosing (global rail 19).

ALREADY EXISTS, do not rebuild: the policy.install payload shape at live-dispatch-payloads.ts:98 and the operator words at work-labels.ts:44.
definitionOfDone: `ACTIVATION_CHAIN_KINDS` (or the prerequisite table it mirrors) causes the browser Activate card to dispatch `policy.install` before `project.activate`, and the choice between changing COMMAND_PREREQUISITES and changing ACTIVATION_CHAIN_KINDS is STATED with its reason in the completion record. If COMMAND_PREREQUISITES is changed, every consumer of that table is enumerated in the plan's owned paths first (global rail 19).

The existing Playwright journey `tests/e2e/control-room/activation-fresh-project.spec.ts` (landed by task-ac9d5e2d) passes UNCHANGED against a real daemon at `seed: "NONE"`: all four -- now five -- chain steps carry data-ok="true" and the `goal.create_with_source` that the same draft was refused before activation is ACCEPTED after it. Quote the `pnpm test:e2e:browser` count line. Do NOT weaken any assertion in that spec to reach green; if an assertion is wrong, say so and route it back rather than editing it.

A test asserts the REASON CODE, not just the outcome: with the policy step omitted, `project.activate` still refuses exactly `ACTIVATION_POLICY_UNMEASURED` at layer `DAEMON_ACTIVATION_RECEIPTS`. Verify by removing the new step and confirming that arm goes RED with that code, and quote the red (global rail 1).
`pnpm seed` stays green with its count line quoted -- DEMO_SEED_KINDS already installs policy before activate, and this change must not double-install or reorder the seed's own chain.

Gates quoted WITH their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`. Repo-wide legs are a path-attributed baseline per global rail 3.
taskRails: The refusal is CORRECT behaviour and must stay reachable. `project.activate` refusing ACTIVATION_POLICY_UNMEASURED when the policy receipt is genuinely unmeasured is the daemon failing closed; this row makes the browser SATISFY the prerequisite, never suppresses or defaults the receipt.
Do not weaken tests/e2e/control-room/activation-fresh-project.spec.ts to reach green. It is the row that found this, and an assertion edited to fit the code retires the question unanswered.
Do not add a policy.install button to the UI. The chain is one operator click; the step is internal to it.

(b) THEN APPLY ONE LINE AND ONLY ONE LINE: add `"policy.install",` to `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES["project.activate"]` in apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-sequence.ts:31-35. Change nothing else. (c) RE-RUN `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and ENUMERATE EVERY NEW RED BY FILE AND FAILING LINE in the step note. Any daemon test that builds a ledger WITHOUT `policy.install` and then expects `project.activate` to be offered or admitted will now flip - and that flip is CORRECT behaviour, not a regression. (d) TRIAGE THE LIST AGAINST THE SEVEN NAMED FILES in planningNotes.keyFiles. If every red is inside them, continue. IF A RED LANDS IN A FILE NOT NAMED HERE, STOP AND REPORT with the list - do not take the extra path (global rail 18). THE TABLE, AND THE DECISION BEHIND IT. THE DESIGN CALL THE ROW LEFT OPEN IS MADE HERE - option (a), change `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES`, NOT option (b). Carry this reasoning into the completion record, because DoD-1 asks for it explicitly. WHY (a): the table is not merely incomplete, it is WRONG. The daemon mints the activation witness from MEASURED receipts and the `policy` receipt is the digest of the installed slice set (activation-receipts.ts:38), so `project.activate` genuinely cannot succeed without an installed policy. A table that omits it makes `missingPrerequisites` UNDER-REPORT, which makes `/affordances/read` offer `project.activate` as READY when the daemon will refuse it - the surface offering a step the command path rejects. Fixing the table fixes every derived consumer at once. WHY NOT (b): `ACTIVATION_CHAIN_KINDS`' own docblock (activation-port.ts:25-28) says it is "The daemon's prerequisite order ... not this module's preference. The chain is fixed: a caller cannot reorder it, because the order IS the prerequisite." Adding a kind there alone would make the control room the authority on daemon ordering - the exact drift that docblock forbids. (1) apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-sequence.ts: keep the one-line edit from step 1 and add a short comment beside it in the file's existing voice, naming the receipt that makes it load-bearing (activation-receipts.ts:38) so the next reader does not "tidy" it away. `policy.install` is already a BootstrapCommandKind with `Object.freeze([])` prerequisites at :29, so the `satisfies Readonly<Record<BootstrapCommandKind, readonly BootstrapCommandKind[]>>` constraint is already satisfied - no vocabulary edit and no type widening anywhere. (2) apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/demo-seed-plan.test.ts:97 already reads `expect(COMMAND_PREREQUISITES["project.activate"]).toContain("provider.probe")`. Add the matching `.toContain("policy.install")` on the next line - same file, same assertion shape, same reason, and it is the only daemon-side home that already imports the table for exactly this purpose. Do NOT touch the order sweep at :53-70; step 1 proved it green.

That is why it drifted, and it is why the transcription must be deliberate rather than incidental. (1) activation-port.ts:29-32: insert `"policy.install"` into `ACTIVATION_CHAIN_KINDS` BEFORE `"project.activate"`. Position it in PREREQUISITE ORDER, matching the daemon table exactly - the docblock at :25-28 states the order IS the prerequisite, so a member in the wrong slot is a live defect, not a style question. Extend that docblock with one sentence naming `policy.install` and the receipt that requires it, and say the mirror is hand-transcribed and must be re-checked whenever COMMAND_PREREQUISITES moves. The existing loop at activation-port.ts:108 defaults to `ACTIVATION_CHAIN_KINDS`, so `driveActivationChain` picks the new step up with no logic change; verify that and say so rather than adding code. Put it beside the existing `policy.install` < `policy.validate` arm at :136 so the two policy facts read together. (3) Do NOT add a `policy.install` button or any new UI (row rail 3) - `WORK_KIND_LABELS:44` already carries the operator words and the chain is one operator click.
